The shared upstream cause is the FRZ-80-02 freezer failure, which exposed the lentiviral vector lot LV25-118 to a temperature excursion. Two CAPAs trace back to it:

- **CAPA-26-008** (closed, corrective): replace the FRZ-80-02 compressor. It came from DEV-26-021, recorded as "compressor failure (age-related)."
- **CAPA-26-016** (open, preventive): evaluate a minimum CD3% acceptance criterion at apheresis receipt. It came from DEV-26-027, recorded as "suspected donor-related variability (low CD3% at apheresis)."

**Why the donor explanation does not hold for DEV-26-027**
- The donor CD3% values for the affected engineering runs are normal: ENG26-01 65.3%, ENG26-02 63.8%, ENG26-03 50.9%. Other batches from the same donor pool with normal CD3% ran fine.
- Every affected run used the same vector lot, LV25-118, which was stored in FRZ-80-02.
- Final CAR+ % (day 5 of expansion) for LV25-118 batches shows a clear break at the excursion:
  - Before 20 April (transduced 5 March to 15 April): 29–42%.
  - After the excursion (transduced 22 April onward, including the engineering runs): 5.5–15%. Examples are PD26-024 at 14.7%, PD26-026 at 10.8%, ENG26-01 at 12.2%, ENG26-02 at 5.5%, and ENG26-03 at 7.0%.
- Batches on other vector lots (LV25-104, LV26-007, LV26-021) with the same donor pool stayed in their normal range. For example, PPQ26-02 used LV26-007 and gave 39% CAR+.
- DEV-26-021 records that the viral vector lots were in FRZ-80-02 during the excursion, with a maximum temperature of about -36 °C. The supplier stability statement requires -65 °C or colder.

**Gaps this exposes**
- CAPA-26-008 was closed as "effective – no recurrence." That check only looked at the alarm. It did not address the vector lot already exposed to the excursion, which kept producing low CAR+ product after the compressor was replaced.
- The LV25-118 lot is still listed as RELEASED with storage location FRZ-80-02. The deviation says the contents were moved to FRZ-80-01, so the lot record is inconsistent with the deviation.
- No trace link connects CAPA-26-008 to CAPA-26-016 or to LV25-118. The connection only appears when the batch and material data are checked together.

**A separate overlap, weaker and not the same cause:** DEV-26-011 (door switch misaligned, CAPA-26-012 still open) and DEV-26-033 (operator did not confirm door latch, CAPA-26-015) both involve incubator INC-03. The door-latch link is plausible, but the records do not establish a common mechanism, so I have not treated it as the shared cause.

content.text:
The shared upstream cause is the FRZ-80-02 freezer failure, which exposed the lentiviral vector lot LV25-118 to a temperature excursion. Two CAPAs trace back to it:

- **CAPA-26-008** (closed, corrective): replace the FRZ-80-02 compressor. It came from DEV-26-021, recorded as "compressor failure (age-related)."
- **CAPA-26-016** (open, preventive): evaluate a minimum CD3% acceptance criterion at apheresis receipt. It came from DEV-26-027, recorded as "suspected donor-related variability (low CD3% at apheresis)."

**Why the donor explanation does not hold for DEV-26-027**
- The donor CD3% values for the affected engineering runs are normal: ENG26-01 65.3%, ENG26-02 63.8%, ENG26-03 50.9%. Other batches from the same donor pool with normal CD3% ran fine.
- Every affected run used the same vector lot, LV25-118, which was stored in FRZ-80-02.
- Final CAR+ % (day 5 of expansion) for LV25-118 batches shows a clear break at the excursion:
  - Before 20 April (transduced 5 March to 15 April): 29–42%.
  - After the excursion (transduced 22 April onward, including the engineering runs): 5.5–15%. Examples are PD26-024 at 14.7%, PD26-026 at 10.8%, ENG26-01 at 12.2%, ENG26-02 at 5.5%, and ENG26-03 at 7.0%.
- Batches on other vector lots (LV25-104, LV26-007, LV26-021) with the same donor pool stayed in their normal range. For example, PPQ26-02 used LV26-007 and gave 39% CAR+.
- DEV-26-021 records that the viral vector lots were in FRZ-80-02 during the excursion, with a maximum temperature of about -36 °C. The supplier stability statement requires -65 °C or colder.

**Gaps this exposes**
- CAPA-26-008 was closed as "effective – no recurrence." That check only looked at the alarm. It did not address the vector lot already exposed to the excursion, which kept producing low CAR+ product after the compressor was replaced.
- The LV25-118 lot is still listed as RELEASED with storage location FRZ-80-02. The deviation says the contents were moved to FRZ-80-01, so the lot record is inconsistent with the deviation.
- No trace link connects CAPA-26-008 to CAPA-26-016 or to LV25-118. The connection only appears when the batch and material data are checked together.

**A separate overlap, weaker and not the same cause:** DEV-26-011 (door switch misaligned, CAPA-26-012 still open) and DEV-26-033 (operator did not confirm door latch, CAPA-26-015) both involve incubator INC-03. The door-latch link is plausible, but the records do not establish a common mechanism, so I have not treated it as the shared cause.
